newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on long liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Thursday with long-position holders liquidating their positions, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 21,800 yuan ($2,628) per tonne, losing 150 yuan. It opened at 22,100 yuan and hit a high of 22,110.
July fell 60 to 21,500, August 150 to 21,650, September 200 to 21,700, November 180 to 21,800 and December 200 to 21,800.
Combined volume rose to 45,900 tonnes from 30,340.
Copper opened higher but profit-taking and fresh selling pushed prices steadily down with most contracts closing at their intraday lows.
Traders said many investors took advantage of the LME kerb gains to liquidate their long positions at high levels.
"Large selling orders poured into the market above the key 22,000-yuan level, reflecting the strong pessimism of Shanghai investors," one trader said.
"Volume increased today, indicating it may be a last chance for long-position holders to liquidate," he said.
Physical prices in the Shanghai area dropped to 21,700 yuan on Thursday, losing 100 yuan from Wednesday, due to a lack of commercial buying, traders said.

Traders said copper was likely to drop further in the next few days due to weak market sentiment. "Copper is likely to test the 21,500-yuan level in the next few days, which may trigger speculative buying at low levels," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up. July rose 120 to 13,720, August did not trade, September 60 to 14,080 and October 80 to 14,250.
Combined volume fell to 980 tonnes from 1,710.
